title: Haegue Yang
bio: Haegue Yang was born in Seoul in 1971. She works across media, ranging from room-size sensorial installations, conceptual works, and performative sculptures to paper collages and staging projects, while engaging broad cultural, philosophical, and historical concerns. In her prolific and versatile practice, Yang juxtaposes seemingly oppositional elements, such as industrial fabrication and folk craftsmanship, to explore the affective power of materialities and methodologies and critically examine the notion of modernity. Recent solo exhibitions have been held at Hayward Gallery, London (2024–25), and the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles (2026). Yang’s work has been included in numerous group exhibitions, in addition to the Venice Biennale (2009); Documenta, Kassel, Germany (2012); Sharjah Biennial, United Arab Emirates (2015); Singapore Biennale (2022–23); and Shanghai Biennale (2025). Yang was awarded the 2018 Wolfgang Hahn Prize by Museum Ludwig, Cologne, and the 2022 Benesse Prize at the Singapore Biennale. Yang teaches at her alma mater, the Städelschule, Frankfurt am Main. She lives in Berlin and Seoul.
